description: An investment committee chair must decide whether the bank should purchase a secondary participation in a project-finance loan and finalize the exposure size, purchase price, legal transfer condition, compliance controls, and settlement mechanics, with input from sector research, legal, compliance, and loan operations.

shared_context.S1: A selling bank has offered the institution a secondary participation in a project-finance loan with a face amount of $10,000,000 and an indicative purchase price of 92% of face value.
shared_context.S2: Maya makes the binding investment committee decision.
shared_context.S3: The loan finances a completed regional water-treatment facility and has made all scheduled payments to date.
shared_context.S4: At the committee's standing pre-trade review, the chair takes a round of updates from credit research, legal, sustainable-finance compliance, and loan operations before finalizing the trade.

PF1.text: Jonas completed a recovery and cash-flow review this morning using the borrower's updated operating data: the committee's maximum sound exposure is $6,000,000 and the participation should be bought at no more than 88% of face value; his revised note has not yet been circulated.

PF2.text: Elena found in the underlying credit agreement this week that any secondary assignment requires written consent from the administrative agent before settlement; this transfer condition is not in the trade ticket template.

PF3.text: Ravi confirmed in a compliance memo received yesterday that this facility falls within the bank's enhanced sustainable-finance review perimeter, requiring enhanced due diligence and a quarterly environmental-impact certificate; the compliance checklist has not yet been updated.

PF4.text: Tessa confirmed with the custodian this morning that this participation can settle only on T+5 business days into a segregated custody account because the seller's agent requires prefunded delivery; operations has not amended the draft settlement instructions.

acceptance_conditions: The participation must be purchased with a face amount of exactly $6,000,000 at a purchase price of exactly 88% of face value.
Written administrative-agent consent must be required before settlement.
Enhanced sustainable-finance due diligence and a quarterly environmental-impact certificate must both be required.
The trade must settle on T+5 business days into a segregated custody account.

The purchase must be approved and the settlement must include commitments for agent consent, enhanced sustainable-finance review, quarterly environmental certification, and segregated-account prefunding.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'agent_consent_before_settlement' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'enhanced_sustainable_finance_review' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'quarterly_environmental_certificate' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'segregated_account_prefunding' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF4' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The public offer supports buying the full $10,000,000 at 92%, while PF1 changes the purchase to exactly $6,000,000 at exactly 88% and supplies the credit basis for approving that smaller, cheaper exposure.
The draft trade ticket has no transfer condition, while PF2 changes agent_consent_required to true and adds the agent-consent-before-settlement commitment.
The public facts contain no special sustainable-finance controls, while PF3 changes both compliance flags to true and adds the enhanced-review and quarterly-certificate commitments.

The draft contains no confirmed settlement mechanics, while PF4 changes settlement_days to exactly 5, changes settlement_account_type to segregated_custody, and adds the segregated-account-prefunding commitment.
